text.p: Authentic Fitness Corp. reported a loss Thursday and said it will exit the skiwear and discount outlet businesses to focus on its successful Speedo Authentic Fitness store chain and designer swimwear.

The Los Angeles-based company posted a loss of $36.1 million, or $1.77 a share, in the fourth quarter ended July 6, compared with profits of almost $7 million, or 32 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues fell to $90.5 million from $97.4 million.

For the fiscal year, Authentic Fitness had a loss of $40.9 million, or $2.08 a share, compared with profits of $19.5 million, or 90 cents a share, in fiscal 1995. Revenues rose to $309.6 million from $266.1 million.
The results include fourth-quarter pre-tax charges of $15.5 million to exit its skiwear business, and $2.0 million to terminate a merger agreement with Warnaco Group Inc. in July.

Authentic Fitness also took a pre-tax charge of $12.4 million in the quarter to close four of the company's Catalina Swimwear Outlet stores, which sell close-out swimwear, and to transfer the leases for the remaining four Catalina outlets to Warnaco.
Net sales for the Speedo brand rose to $162 million for the year ended July 6 from $144 million in the previous year, boosted by its visibility at the Olympic Games in Atlanta, the company said.
The designer swimwear business, including Anne Cole, Catalina, Cole of California and Oscar de la Renta brands, saw sales rise to $80.7 million from $68.6 million in fiscal 1995.

The retail division, which includes the growing chain of Speedo Authentic Fitness stores, saw net sales grow to $38.1 million from $20.4 million over the fiscal year. The division operates 114 stores and plans to open another 30 outlets before Christmas, the company said.
The Speedo division's operating results had been hurt by the bankruptcy of Herman's World of Sporting Goods, one of Authentic Fitness' largest customers, in May.
Authentic Fitness' stock fell 50 cents to $11.375 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
